comments.body:
## Solution written to solution.tex

This is the proof-task for rm-01490: closed-form formulas for F(S), g(S), t(S) of a proportionally modular numerical semigroup S in terms of its minimal generators {n_1<...<n_e}.

What I established (all proofs complete and gap-free):

1. Apery-vector framework. With m=n_1 and Apery vector w_r = min{ s in S : s = r mod m }, I prove from scratch:
- F(S) = max_r w_r - m;
- g(S) = (1/m) sum_r w_r - (m-1)/2  (and that it is a nonnegative integer);
- t(S) = #{ r : w_{(r+n_j) mod m} != w_r + n_j for all j }, via a clean three-way equivalence
  (i) w-m in PF(S)  <=>  (ii) w is preceq_S-maximal in Ap  <=>  (iii) w+n_j not in Ap for all j,
  and the resulting bijection PF(S) <-> maximal elements of Ap.

2. Exact algorithm (Dijkstra on the Apery graph on Z/mZ) computing the Apery vector from the generators; proved correctness, termination, complexity O(e*m*log m). This makes all three invariants explicit, finite, fully-specified functions of the minimal generators.

3. Elementary closed forms for e<=2: e=1 gives S=N (F=-1,g=0,t=1); e=2 with p=n_1<q=n_2 gives F=pq-p-q, g=(p-1)(q-1)/2, t=1, with full proof via the explicit Apery set {0,q,...,(p-1)q}.

4. Proportional-modularity specialisation: proved S([b/a,b/(a-c)]) = {x:(ax) mod b <= cx}, giving the explicit arithmetic description w_r = min{ x = r mod m : (ax) mod b <= cx }, reducible to a finite case split over the <= b/gcd(b,m) sub-progressions; hence a genuine closed form in (a,b,c,m), and thus in the generators.

Honest scope: For e>=3 there is no uniform finite algebraic (polynomial / bounded-degree quasi-polynomial) formula for F in n_1,...,n_e (Curtis). The structural obstruction is verified: minimal generators of proportionally modular semigroups need not form a Bezout sequence and need not have coprime consecutive terms (e.g. <3,8,10> is proportionally modular with gcd(8,10)=2). The correct general closed form is the Apery-vector function above; the manuscript states this precisely rather than overclaiming a single algebraic formula.

Numerical verification: algorithm + all three formulas matched brute force on 180+ random proportionally modular semigroups (up to e=7); e=2 closed forms verified on 300 random coprime pairs; the modular description verified exactly across all (a,b,c) with 2<=a<=11. LaTeX environments and all ref/label cross-references balanced and resolved (no toolchain to compile; checked structurally).
